key_insight: A DFT-trained high-dimensional neural network potential can accurately capture phase stability, defect energetics, and finite-temperature structural evolution in martensitic NiTi.
engineering_relevance: This enables large-scale atomistic simulation of shape-memory alloy behavior over nanoseconds and hundreds of thousands of atoms, supporting design of NiTi components with better transformation and deformation performance.
method: Trained an HDNNP on density functional theory data for NiTi martensite
Validated equilibrium structures, elastic constants, stacking-fault energies, and vibrational spectra
Used molecular dynamics to study temperature-dependent unconstrained structural evolution
evidence_signal: The abstract reports close agreement with DFT, including meV/atom-level stability differences between B19' and B33 phases and an anisotropic stacking-fault landscape.
watch_item: Transferability may be limited to structural motifs and temperature ranges well represented in the training data, so extrapolation to unseen defects or compositions should be checked carefully.
paper_title: A high-dimensional neural network potential for finite-temperature phenomena in NiTi martensite
